observacoes: Cenario mais simples e delimitado dos 9 — um unico tipo de usuario, fluxo central bem definido (abrir-comparar-calcular), exclusoes explicitas e incomuns (contas de usuario, seguranca, rede). RNF raso, parecido com o BECS. Conteudo em ingles porque o cenario-fonte e em ingles (mesma convencao dos gabaritos RAGAS existentes).

em_escopo: Opening a pair of fingerprint files
Viewing the image with minutiae points overlaid
Selecting corresponding points between the two prints and calculating the spatial deviation
Viewing details of an individual minutia (x/y position, angle, classification, annotations)
Saving the session as a reopenable session file
Exporting a table-format log (e.g., openable in Excel) with the compared pairs and calculated deviations
fora_de_escopo: Marking/filtering pairs by a deviation threshold and exporting filtered minutiae — nice-to-have, not required for the first version
User accounts, per-user permissions, and security layers
Simplifying the interface for non-expert users
Ongoing developer support after delivery (prototype/beta-stage tool)
premissas: PA-01: Users already have prior familiarity with minutiae and EBTS-format files.
PA-02: [INFERRED] The tool runs as a local desktop utility, with no need for server installation.
restricoes: REST-01 (Scope): It is a prototype/beta-stage tool, not intended for general release nor for ongoing developer support after delivery.
REST-02 (Technical): The system must operate entirely offline and locally, with no dependency on network or server.

stakeholders.descricao: Biometrics researcher (academia, government labs, industry) — the sole user type, already familiar with minutiae and EBTS files; the interface does not need to be simplified for them.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: The pair marking/filtering-by-deviation-threshold and filtered export feature is optional (nice-to-have) — only the open-compare-calculate flow is required for the first version.
The tool must operate entirely offline and locally — network or server communication is not permitted.
The interface does not need to be simplified for non-expert users — the target audience already understands minutiae and EBTS files.
User accounts, per-user permissions, and security layers are explicitly out of scope.

requisitos_funcionais.descricao: The system must allow the researcher to open a pair of fingerprint files.
The system must display each fingerprint image with its minutiae points overlaid.
The system must allow the researcher to click a point on one print and the corresponding point on the other print.
The system must calculate and display the spatial deviation between two selected corresponding minutiae points.
The system must allow the researcher to click an individual minutia and view its details (x/y position, angle, classification, annotations).
The system must allow the researcher to save the current session as a session file that can be reopened later.
The system must allow the researcher to save the session as a table-format log file (e.g., openable in Excel), listing the compared pairs and calculated deviations.
The system must allow the researcher to mark/filter deviation pairs by a threshold entered during the session — optional, nice-to-have (see RN-001).
The system must allow the researcher to export, to a new file, only the minutiae that pass the threshold filter — optional, nice-to-have (see RN-001).

requisitos_nao_funcionais.descricao: The system must operate entirely offline and locally, without requiring any network or server communication.
requisitos_nao_funcionais.metrica_aceitacao: All core functions (open, compare, save) work with the network disconnected

requisitos_nao_funcionais.descricao: The tool, even at prototype/beta stage, must be stable enough for an experienced researcher to rely on it without ongoing developer support after delivery.
requisitos_nao_funcionais.metrica_aceitacao: [TBD] — scenario does not define a failure rate or stability metric

historias_de_usuario.descricao: As a biometrics researcher, I want to open a pair of fingerprint files, so that I can compare their minutiae.
As a biometrics researcher, I want to see minutiae points overlaid on the images, so that I can visually identify corresponding points.
As a biometrics researcher, I want to click matching points on both prints and see the calculated spatial deviation, so that I can objectively measure how much the minutiae drifted between captures.
As a biometrics researcher, I want to click an individual minutia and see its details, so that I can inspect it closely.
As a biometrics researcher, I want to save my session and reopen it later, so that I can continue my work without losing progress.
As a biometrics researcher, I want to export a log with the compared pairs and deviations, so that I can analyze the results in a spreadsheet.

casos_de_uso.descricao: Compare fingerprint pair — the researcher opens two files, views the overlaid minutiae, selects corresponding points, and the system calculates and displays the deviation.
Save and resume session — the researcher saves the current session to a file and reopens it later to continue the work.
Export comparison log — the researcher exports a table-format log with all compared pairs and their deviations.

criterios_de_aceite.descricao: Given two fingerprint files open with minutiae overlaid, when the researcher clicks a point on each print, then the system calculates and displays the spatial deviation between them.
Given a selected minutia point, when the researcher clicks it, then the system displays its x/y position, angle, classification, and any annotations.
Given an active session, when the researcher saves it as a session file, then the session can later be reopened with all prior comparisons intact.
Given a completed session, when the researcher exports the log, then the file lists all compared pairs and their calculated deviations in a table format openable in a spreadsheet.
Given the tool is running with no network connection, when the researcher performs any core operation (open, compare, save), then the tool functions normally without requiring network access.
